# Migrate existing work

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_guides.py; edit src/, then regenerate. -->

This document contains the complete route, story template and execution rules. Read it fully before acting; do not fetch the router, CORE or the other route unless your task changes. Examples and review history are optional.

Use one guide commit: record a commit-pinned link's SHA; otherwise resolve the supplied branch/tag once and read this document at that SHA. Reuse content already fully present and verified at the same SHA; reread only if changed, truncated or provenance is uncertain. API clients must pass the SHA explicitly. Record this document path, SHA and route in the story. Refresh deliberately and reconcile changed rules; never mix revisions.

If required content is missing, inaccessible or incomplete, report it and stop dependent work; do not guess or silently substitute an older copy. Continue independent authorized work only when the gap cannot invalidate it. This guide grants no authority to build, deploy, spend, share externally or change criteria. A link supplies neither inaccessible chat history nor permission. Infer inputs and existing authority from available context; ask only for unresolved information needed for the next action.

## Route

1. Inventory the latest story, comments, criteria, decisions, design, research, code and evidence. Confirm source revisions, destination repository/folder, branch, concurrent work and existing authorization. Keep a compact source revision → destination/reference → disposition map for material artifacts, decisions, evidence and links in existing story history where practical. Use opaque references for restricted sources. Read relevant prior chats only where they resolve gaps. Distinguish observed results, historical reports, proposals and model opinions; another project’s state is not this project’s evidence.
2. Capture the current ClickUp description verbatim as historical evidence before replacing it. Keep client-identifying originals in approved restricted storage, with an access-controlled mapping to sanitized parameters. Preserve existing attachments and material history. Do not move private content into public Git history.
3. Populate the story template below from the inventory. Preserve agreed criterion IDs and wording, decisions and useful artifact links. Compare source and destination criteria and classify every difference, including sanitization. A missing, inaccessible or unauthorized alteration to a required criterion blocks migration completion. Do not invent evidence, approvals, names, URLs or model identities. Reconcile conflicting facts rather than overwrite them.
4. Reconcile each step against evidence. Keep valid completed work complete; do not restart it merely because the format changed. Reopen checks affected by changed inputs or criteria and leave unverified results NOT RUN. Retain previous execution records, blockers, fixes and review dispositions. Select the next eligible step using the shared rules below.
5. Apply the shared rules below for publication checks. Read back the published revision and verify access to the folder, story and required evidence. Confirm authority to edit the ClickUp item; refresh its text/comments immediately before writeback and reconcile intervening changes. Replace the current description with the two GitHub links; retain the short title/ID, applicable grouping/filtering fields and synchronized owner/date/status fields from their authoritative sources. Read back the result. Preserve originals; mark prior current locations historical or superseded only after the new links and required access work for the intended reader. Keep a recoverable prior reference if the transition fails, and do not maintain two competing current stories.
6. Record the migration revision, source references, differences, preservation checks, unresolved gaps and next action in story history. Reconcile current-state, next-action, configuration and decision statements across retained documents against their authoritative sources. Verify required restricted-context retrieval before claiming portability; record unresolved map/access gaps. Execute only remaining work already authorized. A migration does not transfer prior client permissions, fixture reservations or acceptance to a new environment. Failed synchronization remains an explicit blocker, not a claimed success.

For mixed work, migrate existing scope first. Put genuinely new scope in a separate linked story unless existing user authority permits extending the original criteria; record authorized extensions as material changes with affected checks. For a new story, check for existing related work before creating a duplicate; use the template below, define stable observable criteria, preserve agreed brief requirements and label new interpretations as proposals; establish outcome, scope, exclusions and concise solution, then plan bounded steps using the shared rules. Use MIGRATE+NEW only for an authorized extension within one story. Otherwise record MIGRATE on the migrated story and NEW on the linked new story, each with this guide path and SHA and a link to the other. Retain both scopes clearly. Confirm the destination and authority before creating any repository or ClickUp item; stop only unresolved dependent writes. Do not reread the new-work guide merely for mixed scope.

## Working agreement

Refresh the current story, relevant comments, decisions, dependencies, evidence and authority. When delegating an external change to another chat or agent, include a retrievable reference to the originating human instruction, the authorized action/destination and any visibility assumption. The receiving executor verifies that source; a handoff is not new authority. Keep private authorization references restricted. Reuse accurate work; distinguish facts, historical reports, proposals and reviewer opinions. Never invent identities, results, approvals, URLs or implementation. Keep agreed criterion IDs and wording; material changes need reasons, applicable authority and affected rechecks.

When upgrading an existing story to a newer guide, record both guide commit SHAs, compare changed rules and map affected checks. Preserve prior results as historical; retain still-valid evidence, reopen affected checks, and mark checks not yet performed NOT RUN. Do not silently rewrite the guide provenance or restart completed work.

Keep the story understandable on its own, with concise solution/decisions and links to useful detail. Separate design, research, debugging, planning or evidence files only when their detail or lifecycle merits it. There is no fixed document count or word limit. A typical work-item folder starts with `story.md`; add other artifacts as needed, not empty scaffolding that suggests progress.

ClickUp holds the short story title/ID, epic or parent grouping, ownership, dates, status and applicable priority, categories, flags and labels for filtering and understanding the work. Its description contains the GitHub story-folder link and story-file link. Keep requirements, acceptance criteria, solution/design, execution checklists, research and QA evidence in GitHub and reference them by link when needed. Keep filtering fields concise; avoid copying delivery content into custom fields or comments. Preserve historical source snapshots under the migration rules. GitHub holds the detailed record. Execution evidence governs delivery status; cited human decisions or designated assignment fields govern ownership. Reconcile conflicts and keep unresolved ones visible. Do not maintain competing current stories; preserve historical snapshots.

Use relevant official platform documentation and identify the supported claim and source section/version. Verify actual target metadata, edition, API version, access and behavior before relying on it. A URL proves neither compatibility nor runtime success. A new client/laptop supplies its own configuration and evidence: permissions, acceptance and fixture reservations do not automatically transfer.

## Privacy, publication and links

Keep client identities, instance URLs, real records, credentials and restricted evidence outside public Git. When sanitizing, preserve meaning with named parameters and a restricted mapping; compare source and published criteria and classify every difference. Missing or unauthorized changes to agreed criteria block completion. Use placeholders/synthetic data and an approved restricted index with opaque references, access owner and retrieval instructions. Keep restricted originals and the mapping outside the repository in an approved access-controlled location; the index identifies its access owner and retrieval procedure without exposing sensitive paths publicly. Ignored local/private/reviews paths are only an accidental-add safety net, not approved private storage by themselves. Do not invent public chat links. Missing or inaccessible required evidence remains a gap. Before claiming a portable handoff, verify that the intended authorized executor can retrieve required restricted context using the recorded access owner and mechanism; a pointer to one laptop is not enough.

Before publishing, inspect files/diff, names, commit/branch text, author metadata and history for unauthorized disclosure. `.gitignore` does not remove tracked content or history. Do not falsify author identity. Coordinate the branch, preserve concurrent edits, publish only to the authorized repository and read back saved content and links. Report synchronization failures with a durable local record; never claim success without readback.

Use mutable links for current story/folder and immutable commit/blob references for reviewed inputs and evidence. Label draft branches; verify access as the intended reader. Before replacing any existing ClickUp description, confirm edit authority and capture its current text verbatim (restricted if client-identifying). Account for its criteria in the source/destination comparison. Refresh immediately before writing and reconcile intervening edits. If refreshed text differs from the capture, preserve the refreshed text verbatim and compare/classify its criteria before replacement; replace only after the GitHub files/links are verified, then read back the saved description and fields. Do not use description length or perceived importance to skip preservation.

If the ClickUp item or access is missing, record synchronization as Pending with the reason and needed item/access/authority; request missing information once and retain the gap until resolved. Do not invent an item or create one without authority. Continue independent authorized GitHub work and report its publication separately; do not claim ClickUp synchronization or overall completion while a required sync remains unresolved.

## Copyable story

Replace placeholders with facts, **Pending — missing item**, **Blocked — dependency/resume condition**, **NOT RUN**, or **N/A — reason**. Unknown is not N/A. Keep these concerns covered without mechanically repeating irrelevant sections.

Guide: <consumed guide path/link @ verified commit SHA; route NEW, MIGRATE, or MIGRATE+NEW>
Revision/status/as-of: <revision; documentation/build/test/acceptance states separately>
Origin: <permitted source reference/version; restricted index if necessary>
Accountable owner: <actual person or Pending>

<Independent verification: NOT RUN/Pending/result. Human acceptance: required/not
required/Pending — requirement unknown, with source; actual decision remains Pending until received.>

<Scope, exclusions, baseline facts, assumptions and dependencies.>

## Platform access check

For stories that read or change an external platform, put **Verify platform access** first in the Execution table. Make platform discovery, review, build, testing and writes depend on this check. Keep existing task IDs when adding it to a migrated story.

- **Choose the tools.** Use the approved platform MCP or CLI for backend operations and backend tests. Verify each tool the story will use against the intended account and environment with a minimal read-only probe. Use Playwright or another browser tool for tests of the user journey and user acceptance, acting as the intended user. Browser sign-in also supports tool authentication when needed.
- **Salesforce.** Verify both Headless 360 MCP and Salesforce CLI against the intended org. Start with MCP: discover, describe, then dispatch_readonly. For CLI, check `sf org list --json` privately and run a read-only API check such as `sf org list limits --target-org <ALIAS> --json`. Use MCP first for org work and the verified CLI as appropriate. Writes require existing authority. If a check fails, open only the matching recovery guide at this guide revision: [MCP setup and recovery](../docs/salesforce-mcp.md) or [CLI setup and recovery](../docs/salesforce-cli.md). If both pass, skip the recovery guides.
- **Record the result.** Record the tools, target environment, checks, results and time. Keep private identifiers and credentials in restricted storage. If a required connection fails, record the exact error with sensitive values redacted and block dependent steps until rechecked. Recheck when the executor environment or authorization changes. Changes to OAuth scopes or security settings require explicit authorization.

## Executors and bounded execution

One assigned executor per step; split meaningful human/AI/automation handoffs. The accountable human may differ. Unresolved required assignment blocks dispatch.

- **Human:** actual person and action/decision.
- **Automation:** deterministic workflow/script/tool, version, trigger and accountable operator; AI judgment is not automation.
- **AI:** record **Model** and **Reasoning** using the IDE's names. Follow user/project choices and existing system constraints. Otherwise choose the model by task: routine work → economical; implementation → balanced; difficult debugging, analysis or consequential review → more capable. Set reasoning separately to match task difficulty. Prefer task-relevant quality, then cost and speed. Use the model's supported setting, such as Low, Medium, High or Extra high; write Default when the tool manages reasoning, or Auto when it selects the model. Note any selection change in the task result.

Examples, not fixed assignments (checked 13 November 2026): [Meta Muse Wonder](https://research.meta.ai/blog/muse-wonder); [Google Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Argon or Carbon](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models); [Anthropic Claude Haiku/Sonnet/Opus 5.5 or Fable 5.2](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview); [OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra/Sol or GPT-6 Astra](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/model-selection). Example task entry: `AI · GPT-6.1 Terra · High`. Reasoning labels are tool-specific. Use [Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models) for comparison when needed; project evidence takes priority.

Consider [TypeSafe Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/coding-agents), a decision model, for bounded categorization, routing, scoring and checks against supplied evidence when you need structured answers instead of generated text. Supply clear criteria, test representative cases and handle uncertain/no-match results; use code for exact calculations, generative models for writing and complex reasoning, and preserve existing approval authority.

**Reconcile → select one eligible step → execute → verify → record → recompute → repeat.** Eligibility requires validated inputs/dependencies, executor, authority and budget. Expand only the immediate step; keep later steps concise. Continue independent work only if pending decisions cannot invalidate it. Preserve completed contracts/results inline or by link before expanding the next step. A tool success or subagent report alone is not acceptance evidence.

For concurrency, use a coordinator or atomic shared claim: record step/files, executor, start and expected duration; read back the successful claim. Conflicting claimants wait. Without reliable coordination, use one writer for that scope. An overdue claim does not authorize takeover: establish that the prior executor stopped, inspect partial effects and record reassignment. Refresh before writeback; inspect uncertain writes before retry. Set proportionate time/cost/retry bounds and change the hypothesis before repeating failed attempts.

Check results: Pass (observed expected result with evidence), Fail (observed mismatch with evidence), NOT RUN (check not performed), or N/A — reason (check legitimately inapplicable). Missing knowledge is Pending with a reason, not N/A; a failed criterion cannot be retired this way. Human acceptance requirement is required, not required, or Pending with reason; its actual decision is Pending, accepted, or rejected, with source.

Step states: Pending; In progress (executor/time); Rework (executed check failed); Blocked (specific dependency); Complete (checks passed with evidence); N/A (irrelevant, with reason); Superseded (reason and existing replacement ID). Unknown is not N/A. Neither N/A nor Superseded retires a failed criterion. Evidence governs summaries; changed inputs/criteria reopen affected checks.

## Review and acceptance

Run user acceptance checks through Playwright or another browser tool as the intended user. Record the entry point, user role, actions, expected behavior and observed result. Use MCP/CLI for backend checks and supporting state verification. An inaccessible page or missing action leaves the dependent user journey unverified. Record human acceptance separately from test execution.

Check both human readability and AI execution precision; one reviewer may wear both hats, clearly labeled as maker review when applicable. Human-reader perspective is not human acceptance. A required independent checker must be fresh and inspect actual evidence against frozen criteria. Mockups/model opinions do not prove implementation.

For requested/needed review, send only permitted context: precise question, exact revision, criteria, relevant artifact/evidence, and bounded output structure. Ask for findings with location, impact, correction and verification. Record reviewer, model and reasoning, scope, findings, dispositions and affected rechecks; verify advice before acting. Reuse unchanged valid reviews. Access/model/transmission failures are blockers, not verdicts. Preserve required independent and human acceptance separately; do not invent approval gates or approvals.

For code changes, choose repeatable checks for the changed behavior and its material failure paths. Record the revision, runtime versions and observed results. Verify findings against agreed behavior and reproducible cases. Record confirmed defects and unresolved findings. Send policy questions to the decision owner before changing behavior. Review findings inform decisions. Passing checks require observed results. Where warranted, retain a regression test and rerun affected checks on the repaired revision. Check transaction, access and recovery boundaries touched by the change. Use measurements to support performance claims.

The story coordinator, assigned by the accountable human, uses the agreed criteria, risk and repository rules to decide what to check, when and who checks it. Plan this before implementation and revisit it when scope or risk changes. The accountable human owns acceptance policy, business decisions and any required release approval. For material changes to behavior, shared contracts, access, data or recovery, schedule a fresh independent reviewer after the writer's checks and before merge or handoff. Follow any stricter project requirements. Choose a human or an AI permitted by project policy and suited to the risk and context. Record the selected model and reasoning for an AI review. The reviewer inspects the proposed revision and evidence. Repairs reopen affected checks and findings.

Put applicable code checks behind a repository-owned command that works locally and in CI. The story checklist records the check, executor and result. For examples and an optional Python workflow, see [Code quality checks](../CODE-QUALITY.md).

## Supporting detail when needed

For work exploring standard product capabilities through bounded experiments, read [OOTB discovery and experiments](../references/ootb-experiments.md) at this guide revision. Load it only when that approach is relevant; keep the execution checklist in the story.

- **Design/research:** question and AC IDs; verified facts and dated/versioned source sections; approach/alternatives/tradeoffs; contracts/data flow and failure behavior; assumptions, decisions and validation plan.
- **Debugging:** expected/observed behavior, reproducible case/environment; logs, hypotheses and discriminating checks; diagnosis/confidence; exact fix reference; original-failure retest and affected regressions; limits/recovery. Mark hypotheses untested/supported/disproven. A successful command is not proof of a fix. Keep sensitive raw logs restricted.
- **Configuration:** required keys/types/defaults/validation, runtime/tool versions and retrieval mechanism. Commit placeholders/synthetic fixtures; keep real values outside the checkout where practical, otherwise verify local files are ignored and untracked. Use approved secret storage; never print secrets. Label proposed/unrun commands honestly.

Optional [example](../EXAMPLE.md) and [validation/source mapping](../VALIDATION.md) support illustration or audit. This adapts the earlier agreed template v1.3 and Field Guide v1 + addition v1.1; private source references remain restricted, and user instructions govern adaptations.
